question: When deciding whether to spend confirmation opportunities on a close adviser, does treating correlated title pairs as a shared sampling unit improve out-of-fold returns or reduce useless confirmations? This concerns acquiring evidence, not choosing models by group-weighted accuracy.
episodes: Use only the four predictors present on every one of the existing two registered regrouped five-fold allocations. For each possible primary fold, rotate the next two folds for confirmation and last two folds for evaluation. The primary anchor is the single model with largest observed row accuracy; break ties by content identity. Treat each of the three other measured single methods as a separate potential adviser. No names are privileged. Thirty matched opportunities across ten rotations; the rotations reuse development data and are descriptive.
rules: All three policies choose the primary blend share by the same declared row accuracy over [0,.25,.5,1] and tie towards simpler retention. Strict requires positive primary gain. Row-uncertainty and group-uncertainty buy confirmation for a losing/tied positive-share choice only if it repairs at least one error and the loss is within one paired standard error (row units vs connected-title units). Keep the same positive-primary and near-tie deployment rules as the frozen agent. Only two separate evaluation folds score the chosen policy. Count one completed confirmation panel as a request proxy, not new real fits.
decision: For each allocation report questions answered correctly relative to the anchor, confirmation panels purchased, false promotions (negative effect on the last two folds), and missed beneficial proposals. Prefer the cluster change for a future trial only if on BOTH allocations its eval net is at least the row rule's and its requested panel count does not increase, with a strict improvement on either cost or correct responses. No course labels, official test, H2, API or new supervised fits.
